thread:
meera: quick q — hitting a compatibility oddity between the Python SDK and the raw REST API for the /v1/generate endpoint. REST docs show `stop_sequences` omitted when empty, Python SDK serializes `stop_sequences: []` which makes the server treat it differently (it returns a 400 in some models). Anyone else seen this?

alex: yup saw this in a smoke run yesterday. REST expects missing vs null/empty to mean default behavior. SDK passing an explicit empty list is interpreted as "user provided empty stop list" and triggers validation.

jamal: quick note — TS SDK does camelCase `stopSequences` and AFAICT it omits undefined, so TS is fine. Python mapping from snake_case -> JSON is including empty lists by default for some optional args.

sam: can you paste an example of the request payloads?

meera: yeah — from python SDK we got:
```json
{"model": "redwood-xl-1", "prompt": "hi", "stop_sequences": []}
```
vs REST clients that send:
```json
{"model":"redwood-xl-1","prompt":"hi"}
```
The server treats these differently.

alex: thanks. server-side validator currently checks `if 'stop_sequences' in body:` and does strict validation. Should probably treat empty list identical to missing for backward compat.

jamal: that would be the safest patch. But we should also fix the python SDK to not emit empty lists for optional params unless explicitly set by user. Which behavior do we want as the canonical contract?

meera: my preference: API contract = "omitted equals default behavior". SDKs should avoid sending empty containers for optional params. If a user intentionally wants an empty list (explicitly), we still need a way to opt in — but currently no one expects to send an empty stop list.

sam: agree. Breaking change risk low if we change SDK to omit empty lists. But server-side tolerant behavior is easier for older clients. Two-pronged: make server treat empty list like missing, and update python SDK to omit empty lists.

jamal: action plan: 1) server patch (non-breaking) to treat empty list as missing — small change in request validation; 2) python SDK change to not serialize empty optional lists by default; 3) add contract tests and a small e2e with example clients. Can someone own each?

alex: I can own the server patch and add a regression test in API validator. Will do canary rollout to prod cluster.

meera: I'll open the python SDK PR for serialization fix and add unit tests + a changelog note about the behavior (not a breaking change semantically). I'll ping infra for a build.

sam: I'll add an integration test in the compatibility suite that asserts REST vs SDK request bodies for common param combos (present, missing, empty).

jamal: tagging CI: @ci-bot can you run the compatibility suite once server patch lands?

ci-bot: scheduled: compatibility-suite/run (ref: sha 7f2d1b). Will report back on failures. :gear:

meera: one more thing — we also found `max_new_tokens` vs `maxNewTokens` discrepancy: python SDK sends `max_new_tokens: null` sometimes for defaulting. Same pattern. I'll handle those in the same PR.

alex: good call. Let's keep PRs small but group closely related serialization fixes. Also include a comment in SDK docs about when an argument is considered "provided" vs "omitted".

sam: code review ping — @meera please add a line in the API contract doc (internal) that says "omitted == default; empty list == treated as omitted by server". That should minimize future confusion.

meera: will do. Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/412 (draft) — includes unit tests + changelog.

alex: PR for server: https://github.com/redwood-inference/server/pull/2107 (wip) — validator change + validator unit. I'll request canary tomorrow after tests pass.

jamal: once both PRs are green, I'll run the compatibility suite and then we can schedule a small canary release window (low traffic) to confirm production behavior.

meera: thanks all. If anyone has api contract test snippets to add, drop them here. Otherwise I'll follow up when PR is ready for review. :thumbsup:

sam: quick snippet for tests: asserting that request body generated by python SDK when no stop param -> does NOT contain `stop_sequences`. Add that to sdk serialization tests.

alex: noted. Also adding a server regression test that posts explicit empty list and expects same result as omitted.

meera: final note: tagging product for visibility — this could slightly change telemetry (fewer 400s for bad client), FYI @product: no user-facing feature change.

sam: thanks — closing loop for now.
